newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Fazio warns of risks of globalisation.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Fazio warns of risks of globalisation.

text.p: Economic globalisation risks leading to inflation and currency speculation unless individual countries coordinate policies and strengthen their economies, Italy's central bank governor Antonio Fazio said on Monday.
"Globalisation, especially of finance, brings with it new risks," Fazio told a convention in Rome.

"The absence of a centre of gravity on a world level exposes economic systems to currency and interest rate instabilities and to the weakening, at an international level, of currency control, with the risk of inflationary trends.

"We have to face up to this challenge with a renewed effort to keep the fundamental conditions of each economy in order and also by coordinating economic policies and with extra vigilance on financial and credit markets," Fazio said.
Fazio said the best route to stability was "a closer link between currency and the real economy".

He said healthy public accounts and the control of inflation and public debt and the orientation of economic policy towards stability could boost the advantages of a global market and minimise the risks of sudden changes.

Fazio also cautioned that excluding poorer countries from the increasing globalisation of markets could be extremely harmful and called for a greater will to cooperate on the part of stronger nations.
"The response to the risks of the new system must come from the institutional sector," he said.
He noted that "encouraging" progress had been made in the past two years, including a doubling of resources at the disposal of the International Monetary Fund to deal with crises.
